# Plan to clean up the apps/metis code into a standard skeleton

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Fix every finding of the code review of 09/10/2026 (4 blockers, 22 majors, 28 nits) so that `apps/metis` becomes a standard skeleton that the product owner commits: code that follows the conventions, every gate green as recorded by the machine on exactly that code tree, the review package updated.

**Architecture:** Work in the copy outside iCloud `~/metis-run/lanes/cleanup`. Six foundation tasks run in sequence (conventions and the language scanner; one source for the mock data; the test harness; the shared parts of the screens; the contract and behavior of the shell; the API of the design system). Five area-sweep tasks run in parallel, each on its own lane, and then merge back. After that: turn on the blocking gates, build the native gate, run the full `pnpm verify`, do the round-two review, merge into the repo and update the documents.

> **According to the real run:** the foundation tasks did not run strictly in sequence: Task 2 ran in parallel with Task 1, Task 11 in parallel with Tasks 3 and 4, Task 6 in parallel with Task 5; a task that ran in parallel sits on its own lane. The sweep wave has four lanes (Task 6b, 7, 8, 9), not five. Task 9b was added (integration after the sweep wave). Task 10 ran on its own lane after Task 9b; Tasks 12 and 13 ran in parallel. The round-two review (Task 15) came before the one and only full `pnpm verify`, and it produced a fix wave of four lanes, an integration step, two follow-up waves and a final fix wave. Details are in the section "The real run" at the end of the plan; every place where the plan departs from what was built has a note "According to the real run" like this one, and the original text is kept.

**Tech Stack:** Expo (React Native, react-native-web, expo-router), TypeScript, zod, MSW 2, Jest (jest-expo, four projects: iOS, Android, Web, Node), React Native Testing Library, Stryker, Playwright (Chromium, WebKit), Maestro, ESLint flat config, knip, `node --test`.

**Spec:** `analysis/metis-code-review/report.md` (the merged findings, approved by the product owner at FE-27) together with `spec/2026-10-05-frontend-foundation-spec.md` (the spec approved at FE-16). The original findings are in `analysis/metis-code-review/audits/`; each task records the key of the original finding that it closes. Probe evidence: `analysis/metis-code-review/evidences/probes.md`.

## Global Constraints

- Do not run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push`, `git init`. Each task report lists the files that changed.
  - **According to the real run:** none of these four commands ran on the repo. The lanes have no `.git`, so the `Tree:` line of `pnpm verify` says "unknown"; before the final check the controller copied the `.git` folder of the repo (no commit yet) into the main lane so that `git ls-files` could list the tree (453 files of the app and `brand`).
- FE-27: English for code, comments, test names (`describe`, `it`, `test`), and messages of ESLint, of scripts and of every gate. Vietnamese only in `src/**/strings/vi.ts`, in the `NATIVE_NAMES` line of `src/core/i18n/locale.ts`, in the two-language noscript line of `public/index.html`, and on the line right after a comment `lang-exception: <reason>` (only for test data of the Vietnamese version that is not in the dictionary).
- A comment is one English line that states the reason and does not retell what the code does. Forbidden in code and configuration: the ruling ids of the plan (`R-B15`, `R-N27`, `R-T12`, `D-B23`, `FE-23`), `Task <number>`, spec section numbers (`spec 4.4`), wireframe line numbers (`wireframe.css:199`, `css:266`), measurement dates and measurement logs. Allowed: BRD requirement ids (`OVW-01`, `BR-24`, `D-19`) when they name the requirement. A test name keeps the requirement id at the start, because `gate:trace` reads them.
- One source for each value. Mock-data ids come from `IDS` (`src/mocks/fixtures/ids.ts`); names and numbers come from the objects of `src/mocks/fixtures/*`; UI text from `STRINGS` of the dictionary; paths from `ROUTES`; tokens from `tokens`. A hand-typed English sentence used as the reference may only sit in the model tests (`model.test.ts`, `model.*.test.ts`), where it proves that the model composes the right sentence.
  - **According to the real run:** after the round-two review, the exemption shrank to one reference file per area, by path: `src/screens/<id>/model.test.ts` and `src/shell/model.test.ts` (row 76 of "Rulings made during the run"); the other `model.<part>.test.ts` files build sentences from `STRINGS` with `interpolate`, `plural` and `joined`. The reference file types each composed sentence once and reads ordinary labels from `STRINGS`.
- Test layers: the design system proves the look of a component; screens and the shell prove content, links, roles, accessible names and the layout that they set themselves; they do not re-assert the inside styles of the design system, do not walk the element tree (`.parent`, `.children`, child index), and use `testID`.
- The boundary of spec 3.2 stays as it is. `src/shell` gains the role of shared parts of every screen (Task 16 records it in spec 3.1).
- Each task leaves its area green: `pnpm gate:types`, `pnpm gate:lint`, `pnpm gate:format`, `pnpm gate:deadcode`, Jest of the area with 100% coverage, `pnpm gate:tooling` when `scripts/` or `eslint-rules/` is touched. Mutation testing and `gate:web` run at the milestones noted in the tasks.
- FE-26: one heavy job at a time; do not run Jest while Stryker is running; Jest and Stryker in a parallel lane run with `NODE_OPTIONS="--require $HOME/metis-run/cap-cpus.cjs" CPU_CAP=3`; every heavy command runs with `nice -n 19`; do not run tests in `~/Documents`.
  - **According to the real run:** the four lanes of the sweep wave ran Jest with `CPU_CAP=2` (row 9), lane `t6` with `CPU_CAP=3`; the full `gate:unit` ran in the heavy-job slot (while no other heavy job was running) with `CPU_CAP=8`, that is 4 worker processes under `maxWorkers: '50%'`. The iOS simulator and the Android emulator ran at normal priority: an Android emulator running under `nice -n 19` shows the first screen about seven times slower (measured in Task 14).
- FE-18: do not install new packages unless an item of the approved spec needs it and an error line proves it; record it in the task report.
- FE-23: do not cut any requirement of the approved spec; what could not be done goes first in the review package, with a screenshot.
- Add no abstraction that nobody uses: a new helper must have at least two call sites in the task that creates it; a deliberate simplification is written as a `ponytail:` comment stating the ceiling and how to raise it.
- No long dash or short dash (em dash, en dash) in documents and comments.
- Commands run in the `apps/metis` of the lane. RTK traps: `rtk proxy find`, `rtk proxy ls -a`, `rtk proxy pnpm exec jest`; compare files with `cmp` or `diff -u`.

## Review Focus

1. Change one value of the mock data (the customer name "Northwind Furniture Co.") or one sentence of the dictionary ("Open menu"): only the source file changes, no test needs a manual fix, and every "this text must not appear" test still guards correctly because it is keyed to the same expression as its positive test. Task 8 and Task 9 make a trial change and then restore it.
2. Two equal numeric fields in the mock data: each screen has an "all numbers different" variant, and reading the wrong field turns a test red. Task 9 replants the three bugs of the probe of 09/10 and requires red.
3. The Vietnamese version from start to end: no English sentence slips in, no two identical labels leading to two places, composed sentences follow the dictionary template. Task 5 and Task 9.
4. From a workspace that is not HOME to a page outside any workspace (My focus, Approvals, Notifications, Search): the shell keeps the workspace; the first app open uses HOME. Task 5.
5. Error path: a shell that fails to load has a retry button; if the mock server cannot start, the app still renders and reports the error; a request that slips past the mock server breaks the browser test. Task 4, Task 5, Task 10.

## How to run

- Main lane `~/metis-run/lanes/cleanup` (Task 0). Five parallel sweep lanes `~/metis-run/lanes/sweep-<area>` (Task 6b, 7, 8, 9, 11) cloned from the main lane after Task 6; Task 10 runs in the main lane after the five lanes are merged (it needs `contract.yaml` of Task 9, and the web build with Playwright is too heavy to run next to four Jest lanes) by `cp -cR`; each lane has a base snapshot `~/metis-run/snaps/sweep-<area>-base` (`~/metis-run/bin/snap.sh`). Merge back into the main lane with `node ~/metis-run/bin/merge.mjs <base snapshot> <final snapshot> ~/metis-run/lanes/cleanup`; a file changed by two lanes is a conflict, which the controller resolves and then reruns the gates.
  - **According to the real run:** lanes are built with `mklane.sh` (an APFS copy that includes `node_modules`, and after the fix of Task 7 `wireframes/` as well). The lanes that ran: `t2` (Task 2, in parallel with Task 1), `sweep-tooling` (Task 11, cloned from `t3-before`, in parallel with Tasks 3 and 4), `t6` (Task 6, cloned from `t5-before`, in parallel with Task 5), the four lanes of wave 1 `sweep-ds`, `sweep-core`, `sweep-shell`, `sweep-screen` (Task 6b, 7, 8, 9, cloned from `wave1-base` after merging `t6`), `e2e` (Task 10, cloned from `task9b-after`), `guards` and `native` (Tasks 12 and 13, cloned from `wave2-merged`), the four lanes of the round-two fix wave `r2-gates`, `r2-lint`, `r2-shell`, `r2-ds` (cloned from `task12-final`). After each merge the controller ran all the quick gates itself (lesson from merging `t6`: a semantic error that `merge.mjs` did not see turned `gate:tooling` red). The table of lanes and the numbers of each merge are in the section "The real run".
- Machine load (FE-26) while lanes run in parallel: at most four lanes run Jest at the same time, each with `CPU_CAP=2`; no lane runs Stryker or `gate:web`. The controller runs Stryker for the area of each lane when that lane is done and no lane is running Jest.
  - **According to the real run:** Stryker by area ran in full only for lane `t6` (43 files, 100,00) and in part for Task 7 (stopped at 308 of 472 mutants). The plan switched to one whole mutation run after Task 9b (row 49), which stopped at 347 of 1.636 mutants because each run takes about 3 hours (row 53), and then dropped the mid-way run altogether: the only whole mutation run is Task 14 Step 1 on the final tree, and any fix round that changes a source file runs Stryker on that file alone (row 55).
- Run ledger `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-frontend-code-cleanup/progress.md` (in the repo, carried along by iCloud): a finished task has a line `Task N: complete`; the brief `task-N-brief.md` and the report `task-N-report.md` are in the same folder.
- Each task: one opus agent does it, then another opus agent reviews it (reads the diff between the snapshot before and after the task, reruns the check commands of the task, compares with the original findings); if the review does not pass, the implementer fixes and it is reviewed again.
  - **According to the real run:** sonnet did Task 1 (row 8), Task 9b and the fix of the semantic error after merging `t6`; sonnet reviewed Task 1 and a few narrow re-reviews (Task 1 round 1, Task 10 round 2, Task 13 round 1). The controller re-reviewed by planting defects in Task 13 round 2, Task 12 rounds 2 and 3, Task 10 round 3. Each fix round has a narrow re-review that reads only the package of that round (`<task>-fix<N>.diff`). A review ran check commands only when no other heavy job was running; many later reviews only read statically.
- A task report records: findings closed (keys), files changed, check commands run with results (numbers), decisions taken on its own with the cost if wrong.

### Task 1: Conventions and the language scanner

**Closes:** the mechanism part of the blocker "Vietnamese, no convention, no gate" (`apps/metis#code-language-and-ruling-ids`, `tooling#language-of-code`, `src#ruling-id-comments`, `src/design-system+src/screens#reference-comments`); nit `eslint.config.js#styles-file-split` (keep the `.styles.ts` split, record the trade-off).

**Files:**
- Create: `apps/metis/CONTRIBUTING.md`
- Create: `apps/metis/scripts/check-language.mjs`
- Test: `apps/metis/scripts/check-language.test.mjs`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `node scripts/check-language.mjs [path ...]`: with no argument it scans the whole app and `../../.github/workflows`; with arguments it scans only those files or folders. It prints each error on one line `<path>:<line>: <rule>: <excerpt>`, a last line `check-language: <n> problems in <m> files` or `check-language: clean (<k> files)`; exits 1 when there is an error. Exports `scanText(path, text)` returning an array `{ line, rule, excerpt }`. Tasks 6 to 11 run it on their own area; Task 12 wires it up as `gate:language`.

```js
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { mkdtempSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { test } from 'node:test'

import { scanText } from './check-language.mjs'

const rules = (path, text) => scanText(path, text).map((v) => `${v.line}:${v.rule}`)
const VI = 'Ti' + 'e' + 'ng Vi' + 'e' + 't'

test('flags a Vietnamese comment outside the vi dictionaries', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(rules('src/a.ts', `// ${VI}\nexport const a = 1\n`), ['1:vietnamese'])
})

test('allows Vietnamese in a vi dictionary and on the line after a lang-exception', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(rules('src/shell/strings/vi.ts', `export const vi = { a: '${VI}' }\n`), [])
  assert.deepEqual(rules('src/core/i18n/locale.ts', `// lang-exception: native name\nconst n = '${VI}'\n`), [])
})

test('ignores punctuation and symbols that are not letters', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(rules('src/a.ts', "export const a = '+ 2 more · open in WBS ⌘'\n"), [])
})

test('flags plan ruling ids and task numbers but keeps BRD requirement ids', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(rules('src/a.ts', `// see ${'R-' + 'B15'} and ${'D-' + 'B23'}\n// ${'FE-' + '23'}\n// ${'Task' + ' 13'}\n`), [
    '1:plan-reference',
    '2:plan-reference',
    '3:plan-reference'
  ])
  assert.deepEqual(rules('src/a.test.ts', "test('OVW-01 BR-24 D-19 renders', () => {})\n"), [])
})

test('flags spec section numbers but not spec file names', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(rules('src/a.ts', `// ${'spec' + ' 4.4'}\n`), ['1:spec-reference'])
  assert.deepEqual(rules('e2e/web/a.ts', "import './narrow.spec.ts'\n"), [])
})

test('flags wireframe line numbers but not ports or vendor paths', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(rules('src/a.ts', `// ${'wireframe.css' + ':199'}\n// ${'css' + ':266'}\n`), [
    '1:wireframe-line',
    '2:wireframe-line'
  ])
  assert.deepEqual(rules('src/a.ts', "const url = 'http://127.0.0.1:5310'\n// node_modules/msw/lib/index.mjs:19\n"), [])
})

test('the command line exits 1 with one line per problem, and 0 on a clean tree', () => {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'lang-'))
  mkdirSync(join(dir, 'src'))
  writeFileSync(join(dir, 'src/ok.ts'), 'export const ok = 1\n')
  const clean = spawnSync('node', [new URL('./check-language.mjs', import.meta.url).pathname, join(dir, 'src')], { encoding: 'utf8' })

  assert.equal(red.status, 1)
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write `scripts/check-language.mjs`**

```js
// Language gate: code, comments, test titles and tool output are English; Vietnamese lives only in
// the vi dictionaries. It also rejects references into plan files, spec sections and wireframe lines,
// because the people maintaining this code cannot follow them.
// Usage: node scripts/check-language.mjs [path ...]
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, realpathSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join, relative } from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'

const APP = fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url))
const DEFAULT_ROOTS = [APP, join(APP, '../../.github/workflows')]
const TEXT_FILE = /\.(ts|tsx|js|mjs|cjs|json|jsonc|ya?ml|html|css|md)$/
const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(['node_modules', 'dist', 'dist-e2e', 'coverage', 'reports', 'test-results', 'playwright-report', '.expo', '.stryker-tmp', 'ios', 'android', 'assets'])
const SKIP_FILES = [/public\/mockServiceWorker\.js$/, /pnpm-lock\.yaml$/]
const VI_FILES = [/(^|\/)src\/.*\/strings\/vi\.ts$/]
// The checker's own test and the conventions document quote the banned patterns on purpose.
const QUOTES_PATTERNS = [/scripts\/check-language\.test\.mjs$/, /CONTRIBUTING\.md$/]

const RULES = [
  ['vietnamese', /(?![\x00-\x7F])\p{L}/u],
  ['plan-reference', /\b(?:R-[A-Z]\d+|D-B\d+|FE-\d+|Task \d+)\b/],
  ['spec-reference', /\bspec \d+(?:\.\d+)*\b/i],
  ['wireframe-line', /\bwireframes?\/[\w./-]+:\d+|\bwireframe\.(?:css|html):\d+|(?<![\w./-])(?:css|html):\d+/]
]

export function scanText(path, text) {
  const vi = VI_FILES.some((re) => re.test(path))
  const quotes = QUOTES_PATTERNS.some((re) => re.test(path))
  const lines = text.split('\n')
  const found = []
  lines.forEach((line, i) => {
    const excused = i > 0 && lines[i - 1].includes('lang-exception:')
    for (const [rule, re] of RULES) {
      if (rule === 'vietnamese' && (vi || excused || quotes)) continue
      if (rule !== 'vietnamese' && quotes) continue
      if (re.test(line)) found.push({ line: i + 1, rule, excerpt: line.trim().slice(0, 100) })
    }
  })
  return found
}

function* filesUnder(path) {
  const stat = statSync(path)
  if (stat.isFile()) {
    if (TEXT_FILE.test(path) && !SKIP_FILES.some((re) => re.test(path))) yield path
    return
  }
  for (const entry of readdirSync(path)) {
    if (!SKIP_DIRS.has(entry)) yield* filesUnder(join(path, entry))
  }
}

export function check(roots) {
  let files = 0
  const problems = []
  for (const root of roots) {
    for (const file of filesUnder(root)) {
      files += 1
      const shown = relative(APP, file)
      for (const v of scanText(shown, readFileSync(file, 'utf8'))) problems.push(`${shown}:${v.line}: ${v.rule}: ${v.excerpt}`)
    }
  }
  return { files, problems }
}

/* node:coverage disable */
if (process.argv[1] && realpathSync(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  const roots = process.argv.length > 2 ? process.argv.slice(2) : DEFAULT_ROOTS
  const { files, problems } = check(roots)
  for (const line of problems) console.log(line)
  const touched = new Set(problems.map((p) => p.split(':')[0])).size
  console.log(problems.length ? `check-language: ${problems.length} problems in ${touched} files` : `check-language: clean (${files} files)`)
  process.exitCode = problems.length ? 1 : 0
}
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Red test for `useApi`**, with no waiting time used as an assertion: the old answer is held back by a promise that the test resolves by itself.

```ts
import { act, renderHook, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react-native'

import type { ApiResult } from '../core/api/client'
import { useApi } from './useApi'

const deferred = <T,>() => {
  let resolve!: (value: T) => void
  const promise = new Promise<T>((r) => (resolve = r))
  return { promise, resolve }
}

test('an answer for a key that is no longer current never shows', async () => {
  const old = deferred<ApiResult<string>>()
  const load = jest.fn((key: string) => (key === 'a' ? old.promise : Promise.resolve({ ok: true as const, data: 'b' })))
  const { result, rerender } = renderHook(({ key }) => useApi(key, () => load(key)), { initialProps: { key: 'a' } })
  rerender({ key: 'b' })
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.result).toEqual({ ok: true, data: 'b' }))
  await act(async () => {
    old.resolve({ ok: true, data: 'a' })
    await old.promise
  })
  expect(result.current.result).toEqual({ ok: true, data: 'b' })
})

test('retry asks again and shows loading until the new answer', async () => {
  const load = jest
    .fn<Promise<ApiResult<string>>, []>()
    .mockResolvedValueOnce({ ok: false, error: { kind: 'unavailable' } } as ApiResult<string>)
    .mockResolvedValueOnce({ ok: true, data: 'x' })
  const { result } = renderHook(() => useApi('k', load))
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.result?.ok).toBe(false))
  act(() => result.current.retry())
  expect(result.current.result).toBeNull()
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.result).toEqual({ ok: true, data: 'x' }))
  expect(load).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)
})
```

### Common rules for the sweep tasks (Task 6b, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11)

Each sweep task works in its own lane and changes only the files of its own area (the list is in each task). If a file of another area needs to change, write it in the report to the controller and do not change it yourself. A sweep task does not run Stryker or `gate:web`; the controller runs them per the section "How to run". Within the area, every file follows `CONTRIBUTING.md`:

1. Translate comments into one English line that states the reason (keep reasons that have value, for example why the Android language select has opacity 0.01; drop sentences that retell the code); remove every banned reference id; test names become English sentences that describe the behavior, keeping the BRD requirement id at the start.
2. Retyped text: ids through `IDS`; names, numbers, dates through the objects of the mock data or the output of the model; UI text through `STRINGS` (the Vietnamese version through `STRINGS.vi`); a "does not appear" assertion uses exactly the expression of the matching positive assertion.
3. Tests use the shared harness (`mockServer`, `storageMock`, the width constants, `AppFrame`).

Shared oracle of each sweep task (added to its own oracle):

```bash
node scripts/check-language.mjs <the folders of the area>           # Expected: check-language: clean
pnpm exec eslint --rule 'local/no-restated-literals: error' <the folders of the area>   # Expected: exits 0
NODE_OPTIONS="--require $HOME/metis-run/cap-cpus.cjs" CPU_CAP=2 nice -n 19 rtk proxy pnpm exec jest <the folders of the area> --coverage 2>&1 | grep -E "^(Tests|Test Suites):"   # Expected: passes
pnpm -s gate:types && pnpm -s gate:lint && pnpm -s gate:format   # Expected: exits 0
```

The controller, when the lane is done: `nice -n 19 pnpm exec stryker run --mutate "<the non-test files of the area>"` (Expected: score 100%).

> **According to the real run:** the line above ran only in part: Stryker for the area of Task 7 (20 files, 2 processes because three other lanes were running Jest) stopped at 308 of 472 mutants after 37 minutes (0 survived, 18 timed out), because it ran the tests of the first round; the areas of Task 6b, 8, 9 did not run Stryker by area. Instead the implementers planted mutants by hand and required red (Task 8: 20 times, Task 9: 24 then 28 times, Task 6b: 5 times in the fix round), and then the plan switched to one whole mutation run after Task 9b, which was also stopped and dropped (rows 49, 53, 55). Rules 1 to 3 above stay unchanged.

## The real run (10/10/2026, the Mac of user `mrpo`)

The plan ran by superpowers:subagent-driven-development (FE-28), from the main lane `~/metis-run/lanes/cleanup` (an APFS copy of the repo with `node_modules` and `wireframes/`, outside iCloud). The controller gave each task to one agent to do and to another agent to review; when a review did not pass, the implementer fixed it, followed by a narrow re-review that read only the package of that fix round; no stopping to ask the product owner (FE-21, FE-28). None of the commands `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `git init` ran on the repo: snapshots in `~/metis-run/snaps/` (a read-only copy of the code tree at one moment, made by `snap.sh`) took the place of commits, and the review package is the diff between two snapshots (`pkg.sh`, in `~/metis-run/pkgs/`). Run ledger: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-frontend-code-cleanup/progress.md`; the brief `task-<id>-brief.md` (built from the plan by `mkbrief.py`) and the report `task-<id>-report.md` are in the same folder; the waves of round two have `r2-<name>-brief.md` and `r2-<name>-report.md`. The status report sent to the product owner at 16:12: `status-2026-10-10-1612.md` in the same folder.

A lane is a copy of the main lane (or of the repo) at one snapshot, so that a task can run on its own; `merge.mjs` merges back into the main lane three-way, file by file (with `git merge-file`), and the controller resolves any conflict. After each merge the controller runs all the quick gates itself: a lesson from merging lane `t6`, when the merge agent ran six of the seven gates and missed that `gate:tooling` was red because of a semantic error that `merge.mjs` did not see (`scripts/index-html.test.mjs` read the constant `KEY`, which Task 5 had split into `LOCALE` and `WORKSPACE`).

Comparing `cleanup-base` with `final-tree` file by file with `shasum` (in `apps/metis` and `brand`, except `node_modules`, builds and reports): 97 files added, 21 files dropped (including 7 e2e files moved into `e2e/web/24-project-overview/`), 279 files changed; the final tree has 453 files. Outside those two folders there are also `.github/workflows/check.yml` (Task 11) and `apps/metis-rn-guide.html` (Task 9b, Task 16). The list for the product owner to commit: `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-frontend-code-cleanup/changed-files.txt` (Task 16 Step 5).

What the real run added compared with the original plan, each one produced by a review or by a measurement:

- Task 9b (integration after the sweep wave) and the whole chain of fixes of round two: four lanes, one integration step, two follow-up waves, one final fix wave.
- Shell: a retry button on the icon rail; the gray frame of the session dialog made taller on the phone for the shadow; dropped `main.minWidth: 0`; the workspace is forgotten when it returns `notFound` or `forbidden`.
- Design system: `Menu` in a transparent `Modal`, closing on choosing an item, pressing outside, Escape, Tab (web), Back (Android); `HEALTH_MARK`; `ListRow` wraps its end part instead of breaking the name (web: `min-content`; iOS and Android: minimum 88); a line height that keeps descenders and diacritics on Android; the `count` variant; dialog shadow and dropped border.
- Mock data and contract: `UNKNOWN_ID` and `PEOPLE` in `ids.ts`; project page contract with time zone; the mock-data version on the web keeps the request of a page that is leaving.
- Gates: an unknown code tree is a warning and makes a full run exit 1; the exactly-equal floor and `webExpectedFailures`; tracing of browser specs by screen folder; mutation testing for shared test helpers; `gate:native` refuses a dangerous build folder; `restrictions.js`, `literals.js`, `canaries.mjs` split out so as to have tests and to keep the 300-line ceiling.

Environment and traps measured during the run (for the next times):

- Stryker splits `--mutate` on commas: the pattern `{a,b}` matches no file, the score is NaN, exit 0 (an empty pass); `scripts/mutation.mjs` now treats a run with no valid mutant as RED.
- One `pnpm exec prettier --check` printed "All files formatted correctly" while three files were wrong (the controller could not repeat it): read the exit code, prefer `rtk proxy`.
- Running `pnpm exec` from a copy that points `node_modules` through a link makes pnpm rewrite its own record in the main lane ("Packages: -78"); do not run pnpm from such a copy. pnpm 11 also prints "Packages: -78" at the first `pnpm exec` of a few lanes; later runs are still green.
- The agents share the scratch folder of the session and the file of one agent once vanished: each brief names its own subfolder.
- A bare `node --test` through the RTK hook does not print the TAP totals: use `rtk proxy node --test --test-reporter=tap`.
- A Jest process died of SIGSEGV once on this machine (with no red test); the rerun was green.
- The Android emulator running under `nice -n 19` shows the first screen about seven times slower: run it at normal priority. The virtual tablet turns to landscape by itself right after it finishes booting: set `user_rotation 1` once SystemUI is stable and check `cur=1600x2560` right before the flow.
- After `pnpm canary all`, the `dist-e2e` of the lane is the build of the `touch-target` reverse test (a 30 x 30 button planted in screen 24): do not take screenshots or run Playwright by hand on that build.
- zsh does not split a string of commands into several arguments: one `xcodebuild` run and one defect planting failed because of it; the defect-planting tool now puts the file back even when it hits a launch error.
- `diff3 -m` on this machine drops a bracket when merging; `merge.mjs` uses `git merge-file`, and the controller checked: 0 lines of any lane were lost.
- A cold start of the iPhone simulator pushes the one-minute load to 55 to 113 for about 90 seconds; a Spotlight indexing storm pushed the load to 35 and broke one Android run.

## Rulings made during the run

Each `Ruling:` line of the run ledger is a row, in exactly the order of the ledger (the column "Line" is the line number in `progress.md`): what was decided, why, the cost if wrong, exactly the three parts of the ledger, with the task or wave it belongs to. The controller decided on the product owner's behalf per FE-21 and FE-28. A ruling that was replaced or reversed keeps its row, and both rows say which row replaces which. 89 rows: line 12 of the ledger is a title, not a ruling; line 81 is a deferred item with a ruling inside it. Two lane reviews of round two (lines 372 and 376) proposed a few small rulings for the integration step themselves; these are not `Ruling:` lines of the controller, so they are not rows here.
